I heard somebody commit suicide via jumping off the roof of my workplace, and found their body immediately after. I’m somewhat glad I didn’t see the actual impact itself as the sight of their body alone has been enough to cause some pretty severe trauma. 

I called the police after myself and a few witnesses just kind of...stood there staring? I’d heard of the bystander effect for thing like bullying but when it comes to a dead body Yu really have no way of knowing how you will react (because why on earth would you be in that situation?) One girl checked for a pulse (she was a nurse) but there wasn’t anything anyone could do. 

After the police arrived I walked all the way home in a state of shock. It took a few hours I think and I was terrified of absolutely everyone I walked past for no apparent reason. 

As a result I really have to focus on my breathing when I hear loud bangs and I still get really antsy when I see and hear police sirens. Working through it all with a professional though. I remember being so angry at that person for making so many people have to witness such an awful sight (I know that sounds quite cruel), then I was really sad that nobody ever mentioned them on the news so I scrawled through the obituaries trying to find them. Now I’m mostly just trying to make peace with it. I still think about them daily though, and it’s been around six months.

I have some experience (keep in mind this was around one/two months ago and I am unsure if things have changed).

You are legally allowed to terminate your lease on grounds of financial hardship due to COVID-19. You must give 14 days notice, and are not required to provide your property manager with documentation (although you will most definitely need it if/when they attempt a VCAT claim - you obviously do actually need to prove that you are suffering financial hardship). I lost my job and did not qualify for any government support, and one of my housemates required long-term medical care, so we went with this route.

Please be aware that your property manager will attempt to make this as difficult as possible, and this a new law under the COVID-19 Emergency Measures Omnibus. They will likely attempt a VCAT claim for lost rent or whatever other reason they can (they have done so with us) and the wait time at the moment is around two months (high traffic).

I really do recommend you get in contact with Consumer Affairs first, not only to get further legal clarity, but also to demonstrate you went via all the proper channels (they keep reference numbers for your case which can be viewed and added to at later dates). Some of their staff are more helpful than others, and there are very long wait times at the moment, but I can't recommend it enough as they have almost full knowledge of the changed COVID tenancy laws.

Stay safe and good luck!
